analysis:
The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The visible patch adds one row to the environment-variable forwarding table for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP, which is a performance setting: `0` disables load-time shape warmup and `always` skips the shader-cache probe. The new row sits at head line 1751, outside the two supplied text units (lines 1-830). It is documentation-only, so there is no code, authorization, attestation, encryption or protocol change.

I read the supplied text (lines 1-830) for documentation that overclaims security. It describes logout revocation (only HTTP 204 confirms remote revocation, with the local-only case explicitly warned), the encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041; cache settings, directory pinning, no disk certification), the GLM local qualification (it does not advertise the identity to the coordinator), the App Attest enroll guidance (not a grant), and drain/stop behavior. None of it contradicts the canonical threat model. The T-041 cache statements match: encrypted at rest, kill switch DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0, and no disk firmware certification claimed.

The new env var affects load-time warmup, not prompt data, keys or cache TTL, scope or encryption, so it does not touch the T-041 detection-hint surfaces. Remaining uncertainty: the actual ModelCalibrationPolicy.swift behavior and the daemon forwarding in LaunchAgent are outside the supplied evidence. The new row is not in the viewed units, so I could not confirm that the forwarded value is validated or that a skipped shader-cache probe has no security impact. This is a question for a source-pass reviewer, not a finding.
